_comment: The core's size budget. The point is not the number: it is that deleting the legacy harness is measurable, so 'the core replaced the harness' is a reading rather than a claim. `coreLines` is a hard ceiling for the new programmatic surface (scripts/core + scripts/store); it follows a recorded measurement, which is how an estimate becomes a reading. `legacyCeiling` is the measurement of everything else and moves in exactly two directions: DOWN whenever legacy code is deleted, which is the only movement that needs no reason, and UP only for shared infrastructure that judges nothing, with its lines named in `_revisions`. It may never absorb a new legacy *gate* — a script that judges an artifact — because that is the defect this number exists to prevent.

_revisions.why: The 9000 was an estimate written before two ports that requirements-preservation.md requires: `scripts/core/manifest.mjs` (rows 9.5, 9.6, 9.7, 9.8, 15.7, 16.11) and `scripts/core/policy.mjs` (rows 7.6 and the promise contract), which took the surface to a measured 10278. This is the estimate being replaced by the measurement, not a legacy ceiling being relaxed: `legacyCeiling` is untouched and still only moves down. The number that measures the change's own claim is `scripts total`, now 38905 against a 9000-line design target reached only by deleting the legacy gates.

The UI baseline the owner asked for after reviewing the first live app, `apps/2026-09-26-teacher-gradebook`. Four files are new surface and nothing else moved: `scripts/core/uiux.mjs` (1287), `scripts/core/settings.mjs` (1253), `scripts/core/localization.mjs` (743) and the shared `scripts/core/baseline.mjs` (91), which is 3374 lines and takes the measured surface to 14124. Three of those are rules that had **no program behind them at all** before this change — the factory's most-recorded failure mode is a rule only a document asserts — so the increase buys enforcement rather than documentation. Recorded honestly as a cost: the core is no longer the lean replacement the 9000 target described, and every future baseline rule costs close to a thousand lines. The direction to watch is `coreLines` per rule, not this total. `legacyCeiling` is lowered in the same edit, from 51500 to the measured 27070, which is the tightening this file is for and can only cause a failure, never hide one.

The owner's instruction after a Gradle build filled his machine's system temp directory and slowed it to a 30-second-to-five-minute start-up: a factory process may make any mess it likes **inside** the repository and may write nothing outside it. The fix is `scripts/lib/scratch.mjs` (72 lines) — the single place that decides where a temporary file goes — plus routing `scripts/lib/gradle.mjs`'s spawn environment through it, plus the 14 files whose fixture sandbox was built in the system temp (four of them on **every** `verify.mjs` run). `checks` grew by 234 measured lines in `scripts/core/build.mjs`: the `build.scratch` sensor, its four pure predicates and the five fixtures that make each of them able to fail. So `coreLines` follows its measurement to 14358, and `legacyCeiling` moves by exactly 159 lines across two halves, named here so the move is auditable: the JavaScript half is `scripts/lib/scratch.mjs` (72), `scripts/test-slot-lock.mjs` (+1) and `scripts/test-kill-path.mjs` (+3), the two files whose temp call needed an extra import line because `hostname` cannot share one with the new binding; the Python half is `scripts/lib/scratch.py` plus the two-line import that the 11 redirected `tempfile` calls across six scripts now need; the last 23 are the `atexit` cleanup that `test-store-studio-completeness.py` gained, because moving its 0.41 GB slot copies out of the system temp made a leak that was already there visible - 20 leftover `studio-sandbox-*` copies measured 8.2 GB, and the suite now removes its own. This is the case the refined `_comment` describes rather than the defect it forbids: the 84 lines judge nothing — `scratch.mjs` reads no artifact, and no fixture sandbox is a gate — so this is a measurement re-taken, not a legacy gate absorbed. The honest cost of the previous revision is recorded too: setting `legacyCeiling` to the exact measurement of that moment made any addition to `scripts/lib` a failure regardless of kind, which is how a ratchet turns into a blocker. The deletion direction is unchanged and still owed: `scripts total` is 41459 against the 9000 design target, and stage 5 of the `reduce-factory-to-core` change is where the legacy gates come out.

The owner's instruction after having to ask repeatedly for subagents to be used at all: the factory's model is that the main chat orchestrates and the work runs in parallel subagents, and in practice one agent did everything serially. The cause was mechanical, not cultural. Four rules under `.cursor/rules/` carried **no YAML frontmatter at all** — `parallel-execution.mdc` (the discipline being violated), `release-gate.mdc` (the phase boundary), `authorization.mdc` (commits, signing keys, uploads) and `differentiator-contract.mdc` — and a `.mdc` file with no frontmatter is attached to no context by Cursor's loader: no `description` to match, no `globs` to scope by, no `alwaysApply` to honour. Measured, not inferred: the ten rules carrying `alwaysApply: true` were exactly the ten that reached a session, and those four were absent from every one. A rule that cannot load is the factory's most-recorded failure mode — `AGENTS.md` names it — except inverted: it is not a rule with no program, it is a program with no rule, and its presence in the tree made the gap invisible. The fix is `harness.rules` in `scripts/core/harness.mjs`: it parses each rule's frontmatter and fails when a rule has none, has no `description`, or declares neither `alwaysApply: true` nor `globs` — the last clause is derived rather than hand-listed, because a rule scoped to nothing and not always-on is reachable only by an agent that already knows to ask for it, and a hand-written list of 'rules that must always load' would be a copy that drifts. Nine inline fixtures drive it, including the negative controls that keep it honest (`alwaysApply: false` with `globs` must NOT fail, so the check is not merely 'alwaysApply must be true') and the parser controls (a description containing a colon and non-ASCII text, a `---` separator in the body). Both directions were observed rather than claimed: before the frontmatter was added the check reported all four files by name, and after it reports 21 rule(s), 14 always-on. So `coreLines` follows its measurement; `legacyCeiling` is untouched, and its direction — down — is unchanged.

The owner's instruction that the review checkpoint must cost nothing but development: no screenshots, no signed build, no signing password before he approves the app. The rule already claimed that boundary; an adversarial audit of it found the claim half true. The four documented entry points do refuse without an approval record, but two sibling entry points produced release work with no machine gate at all: `scripts/store-studio.py` composed the icon, the feature graphic and the screenshot sets and rewrote the app's own launcher vectors, and `scripts/sign-release.mjs --generate` minted a keystore together with the password that unlocks it - the exact violation `.cursor/rules/authorization.mdc` was written from, guarded until now by prose alone. Both now call the same single source of truth the other four use (`checkReleaseApproval` / `release_approval_block`), both were observed refusing on an unapproved slot, and the studio was observed loading the shared wrapper rather than restating the rule. That is the 59-line half, measured: 21 in `sign-release.mjs`, 38 in `store-studio.py`, plus a one-line correction in `publish-privacy.mjs` that also removed a printed falsehood - it told the reader that editing the listing does not void the approval, when the listing is an authored pack input that does. The larger 839-line half answers a different instruction, that the orchestrator must not sit waiting on a dead subagent: `scripts/lib/subagent-liveness.mjs` (329), `scripts/watch-subagents.mjs` (241) and `scripts/test-subagent-liveness.mjs` (269), which classify a worker DONE/FAILED/RUNNING/STALLED from its transcript and a bounded idle threshold. Recorded honestly rather than filed as infrastructure: the 839 judge no artifact, which is the case this field allows, but the 59 do apply a judgement, and they are named here for that reason. What they judge is not a new rule - they import `release-approval.mjs` and hold no approval logic of their own - so the alternative was not a leaner legacy but two unguarded doors into the one irreversible step this factory has. Still open, stated rather than implied: a raw `./gradlew assembleRelease` still signs once a key exists, and a direct in-process import of the leaf writers in `store/render.py` still bypasses its gate. Neither is a CLI entry point, both need a sensor rather than a call site, and no sensor exists yet. The five lines this record adds are its own JSON: `budget.json` lives under `scripts/core/`, so the record is counted by `coreLines`, and it is named here so the move is not mistaken for new logic.

Two owner instructions arrived one after the other, and each closes a rule the factory had only in prose. FIRST: the app's name had no contract at all. `scripts/new-slot.mjs --name "<Title>"` took free text and nothing judged it, so an agent building a utility could call it `Calculator` — the owner's own example, and the reason he asked for the name to be derived from the app's job, audience and market rather than invented. The measured Play rules and the nine naming archetypes are recorded in two new research docs (not counted here: they are `.md`), and the contract now mirrors `economics.json` and `differentiators.json`: `scripts/lib/slot-naming.mjs` (570, legacy) is the single validator, `scripts/check-naming.mjs` (196, legacy) is the CLI gate and the path `new-slot.mjs` validates before anything is written, and `scripts/core/naming.mjs` (286) is the slot check and its 12 inline fixtures. SECOND: the checkpoint wording told the owner to install and test the app. An agent ran `/forge`, wrote some code and stopped to ask the owner to install and confirm it, having verified nothing itself — the owner's correction is that the agent develops the complete app, tests it on the connected phone ITSELF, and hands him a finished product to accept or amend. Twelve files carried that wording (`.cursor/commands/forge.md`, `ship.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules/release-gate.mdc`, `harness/README.md`, `.cursor/skills/run-playkiln/SKILL.md`, `docs/play-console-checklist.md`, `openspec/changes/app-lawn-round-log/tasks.md` and four residual sites inside them); none is counted here, because the measured surface is `scripts/` only. What IS counted is the sensor that makes the device run a claim resolving to a file: `scripts/core/device.mjs` (532) reads `device-verification.json` and cross-checks the recorded sha256 against the built debug APK, which is `apk-provenance.mjs`'s rule applied at the point where it was missing. `scripts/core/index.mjs` grew by 14 lines of registration. `scripts/new-slot.mjs` grew by 90 net. Recorded honestly: 15371 - 14534 = 837 core lines, of which 818 are the two new sensors, 14 are registration, and 5 are this record's own JSON — `budget.json` lives under `scripts/core/`, so a revision is counted by the number it revises, which is named here rather than left to look like logic; 28988 - 28130 = 858 legacy lines, of which 766 are `slot-naming.mjs` and `check-naming.mjs` and 90 are `new-slot.mjs`, the remaining 2 being the check's own line-counting method. The legacy movement is infrastructure and two gates, so it is named rather than filed silently. One consequence stated rather than discovered later: the five slots that already exist carry no `naming.json` and no `device-verification.json`, so they now report `slot.naming` and `slot.device` as UNVERIFIED — which is true, not a false alarm, and is the same treatment `slot.differentiators` gives a slot with no contract. The direction this field prefers is still down, and the deletion of the legacy gates remains owed at `scripts total` 44354 against the 9000 design target.

A regression check for a defect measured on a real device, which the existing sensor had passed. On the Samsung Galaxy A16 (serial R58MB3SGZVL, 1080x2340 @ 480dpi, `settings get secure navigation_mode` = 0, i.e. a 48dp three-button bar) the Round screen of `apps/2026-10-01-lawn-round-log` painted its bottom action bar from y=1875 to the physical bottom y=2340, and from y=2196 down the pixels were `#162B15` — exactly 60% of the bar's own `#254723` on every channel, the system bar's 40% scrim over the app's controls — so the bar's second row was unreadable and untappable. `uiux.insets` returned PASS on that file, because it measured only `enableEdgeToEdge()` and the IME placement: a screen could pin chrome under the system bar and no program saw it. The new leg inside `uiux.insets` fails a source that pins bottom chrome without naming a navigation-bar inset at all — a window-filling `Column` (or one holding a weighted child) whose `Surface`/`Column` child follows a weighted or scrolling child, with none of `navigationBarsPadding()`, `windowInsetsPadding(…)`, `safeDrawing`, `WindowInsetsSides.Bottom`, `systemBars` or `contentWindowInsets` in the file — and it resolves the sibling composable call to its same-file declaration, so the `RoundActions(…)` shape that actually shipped is caught rather than only a literal `Surface`. 228 measured lines in `scripts/core/uiux.mjs`: the three predicates, `topLevelChildren`, `declaredBarRoot`, `barChild`, `pinnedBottomBar` and `bottomChromeFindings`, plus the extended `uiux.insets` fixture leg. Observed in both directions rather than claimed: driven directly, the leg reported the finding on the un-inset bar (and on the same-file-composable bar) and reported nothing on the same bar with `navigationBarsPadding()`, on a `Surface` written before the weighted list, or on a lone `LazyColumn` carrying `safeDrawing`; and with the leg temporarily neutered, `uiux.fixtures` failed naming that fixture (`uiux.insets fired=false … expected true, got false`), which is the check proving it can fail. No false positive on the slot the defect came from: `node scripts/verify.mjs --slot lawn-round-log` reports `uiux.insets` PASS over its 26 Kotlin sources, and `uiux.scaffold` stays PASS because the scaffold holds no `LazyColumn` and no weighted child, so the leg cannot reach its condition. The 5 lines this record adds are its own JSON, counted by `coreLines` for the reason the previous entry states.

The owner's report after installing a built app on a real modern phone: text crawls onto the notification panel, text crawls onto the camera, and it hides under the bottom buttons - the writing agent 'writes as if for old phones' - and, in the same breath, that the app is 'just ordinary buttons and ordinary texts' while Android offers far more. The existing `uiux.insets` could not see either half: it measured only that `enableEdgeToEdge(` appeared anywhere and, when a text field existed, that the manifest declared `windowSoftInputMode` and some file named an IME API. Two dated research docs (not counted here - they are `.md`) measured the mechanics: `safeDrawing = systemBars ∪ ime ∪ displayCutout` while `systemBars` contains neither the cutout nor the IME, which is why `statusBarsPadding()` alone collides with a punch-hole camera in LANDSCAPE; `ScaffoldDefault.contentWindowInsets` carries the bars and the cutout but no IME; and a `Scaffold` does not apply insets to content at all, so an unused `innerPadding` is as exposed as no Scaffold - which is precisely what the reference slot `apps/2026-09-26-teacher-gradebook` does at `ui/components/Surface.kt:24`, a real finding this change now reports. `uiux.insets` gained four predicates: edge-to-edge via `enableEdgeToEdge(` **or** `WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(..., false)` (the old check knew only the first, so a slot that opted out the other way was wrongly reported), a `Scaffold` whose content lambda never consumes its `PaddingValues` - in all three binding forms, named, destructured and implicit `it` - a FAIL; an M3 bar with a zeroed `windowInsets`, a FAIL; and two notes inside a PASS (`fillMaxSize` root with no inset and no inset-applying ancestor; bars-only with nothing cutout-aware), because the research rates both medium-to-high false-positive and a noisy sensor is worse than a missing one. A new slot check `uiux.platform` answers the second half: FAIL when the manifest omits `android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback` and when a build file declares an M3 Expressive / `MotionScheme` **alpha** artifact the pinned BOM (`material3 1.4.0`) does not carry, plus seven presence-only notes (splash screen, share / `ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT`, Photo Picker, haptics, `animateItem` / shared-element motion, `SelectionContainer`, autofill `contentType`) that are product-conditional and must never be gates. Five facts were added to `docs/research/measured-facts.json` naming their enforcing check, and the insets source list grew to 31 citations, each asserted present in `docs/ui-ux-standards.md`. Measured, not estimated: 16701 - 15604 = 1097 lines, of which ~1050 are `scripts/core/uiux.mjs` (the four `uiux.insets` predicates with their helpers, the whole `uiux.platform` sensor and its fixture legs), ~35 are `scripts/core/index.mjs` registration, and 5 are this record's own JSON, counted by `coreLines` for the reason the previous entries state. Falsifiability observed rather than claimed: nine mutation legs each reverted one predicate and each turned `uiux.fixtures` FAIL (`30 fixtures`), with the file restored byte-identically, and two defects the worker found in its own predicates while proving that - a `trailingLambda` that read the lambda's own parameter list as the call's arguments, and an ancestor guard that fired on correct paren-less `Scaffold` code - were fixed before the suite was allowed green. `legacyCeiling` is untouched: nothing in this change is legacy. No false positive on the template or the in-flight slot: `uiux.scaffold` stays PASS and `node scripts/verify.mjs --slot 2026-10-01-lawn-round-log` reports both `uiux.insets` and `uiux.platform` PASS, while the pre-baseline reference slot prints the real `Surface.kt:24` finding as a non-gating note.

Two owner instructions arrived together after he installed a built app and looked at it: the icons are hand-drawn imitations and a modern app **downloads ready-made, professional icon sets**, and the palette is unaesthetic — a high-chroma lime accent on a dark green field reads as neon. This revision is the icons half; the palette half is a separate change with its own sensor, and it is registered separately so neither record has to carry the other's numbers. The measured defect is not an opinion. `apps/2026-10-01-lawn-round-log` ships launcher art whose three vectors are identical in geometry to `scaffold/android-compose`'s placeholder — foreground (2 paths, `#FFF7ED`/`#FFB86B`), background (3 paths, `#0B3D5C`/`#006C4C`/`#FFFFFFFF`) and monochrome (1 path, `#FFFFFFFF`) — and none of those colours is a role in the slot's own `store/studio.json` palette, so the app about to be handed to the owner had no mark of its own at all. `scripts/core/icons.mjs` (1378) is the sensor and lives in the `icon` group beside the adaptive-icon check: seven legs — `icons.mark` (the declared mark resolves in the Python-owned `MARK_REGISTRY`), `icons.launcher` (the launcher vectors are the slot's own rather than the scaffold's, judged by path geometry and by whether each fill colour is a role of the slot's palette), `icons.provenance` (the `icons/provenance.json` record resolves — schema, SPDX allowlist, every file present and hashing to what it claims), `icons.licence` (each declared SPDX has committed, non-empty licence text), `icons.offline` (no icon artifact is fetched at build or run time), `icons.deprecated` (no deprecated `material-icons-core`/`-extended` coordinate, which the pinned Material 3 no longer carries) and `icons.tint` (UI iconography carries no literal colour; the mark is excluded by design) — driven by 16 inline fixtures. `scripts/core/index.mjs` grew 34 lines: 12 to register the sensor, and 22 for its `reports` list and the assertion that guards it. That list is written **literally** on purpose — `checkIdsFromRegistry` reads the registry as text, so a fact may only name an id that appears there as a literal `id:`, and deriving the list from `ICON_IDS` would look like one source of truth while putting all seven legs out of the ledger's reach. A load-time assertion turns a drift between the two lists into a startup failure rather than a fact that quietly stops being enforced. Falsifiability observed rather than claimed: the live slot FAILs `icons.launcher` on all three vectors, while `apps/2026-09-26-teacher-gradebook`, whose vectors are its own art, fires that leg on none of them and reports only the two provenance rows — the discrimination between 'this slot own art' and 'the scaffold placeholder' is measured, not asserted. `legacyCeiling` moves by exactly 208 and every line is named, because the rule allows only shared infrastructure that judges nothing: `scripts/lib/colours.py` is 67 new lines — the single implementation of sRGB-to-linear, WCAG relative luminance and contrast ratio that `visual-qa.py`, `icon_qa.py` and `store-studio.py` each previously carried as its own byte-for-byte copy; `scripts/lib/icon_design.py` grew 35 for the `mark-stripes` primitives (design data, no judgement); and the remaining 106 are that consolidation plus the pack-writer's palette-inheritance guard across `scripts/store-studio.py`, `scripts/visual-qa.py` and `scripts/lib/icon_qa.py`, which refuses a baseline slot that omits a palette role instead of silently painting another app's colours — the historic behaviour that shipped the reference slot's amber into a green app. Recorded honestly rather than filed as clean: that guard is a judgement living inside a legacy writer, and the core palette sensor is where the same question will be asked where a gate belongs. Its applicability is derived, not hand-listed: the BASELINE date is read out of `scripts/core/baseline.mjs` rather than restated, so the two cannot drift. Two limits stated rather than implied. No slot has an `icons/provenance.json` yet, so every slot now reports `icons.provenance` and `icons.licence` as UNVERIFIED — which is true, not a false alarm, and is the same treatment `slot.differentiators` gives a slot with no contract. And the sensor cannot tell a beautiful icon set from an ugly one: it can only say the set was licence-cleared, vendored and tinted from the theme, which is why the owner still judges the mark and the palette at checkpoint 1. One line outside `scripts/` was corrected in the same change and is not counted here: the slot `studio.json` prose claimed the mark's 66dp ink coverage was `~0.24`, which contradicted `icon_qa`'s own measurement, and now reads the measured 0.1738 against its analytic 0.1714. The arithmetic: 18118 - 16701 = 1417 core lines, of which 1378 are the sensor, 34 is the registration and its literal `reports` list with the assertion that guards it, and 5 are this record's own JSON, counted by `coreLines` because `budget.json` lives under `scripts/core/`; 29196 - 28988 = 208 legacy lines, named above.

_targets.note: The design target. Reaching it means deleting the legacy gates rather than porting them, which is only safe once each one's requirements-preservation row has a proof.
